problem: On a CO-50 medical-necessity denial, a Northwind Imaging denial specialist can today mark an appeal packet ready with no clinical-note reference and no filing-deadline date. CO-50's only allowed next action is to appeal with the coverage policy and a clinical-note reference, and Northwind Health timely filing in this demo is 90 days from the date of service, so a packet missing either element is not actually appealable and can silently miss the payer clock. The workbench needs a CO-50-only readiness gate that fails closed in v1: the ready action is disabled until both items are present, the disabled control names exactly what is missing, the rule lives in the domain layer so a forced transition is also rejected, and a blank deadline never looks safe on the queue. The product must not decide medical necessity, change a diagnosis code, invent a modifier, or write off a balance.
users: Denial specialist - works appealable denials and is the only role that may mark a CO-50 packet ready, and only when the gate passes; cannot override the gate in v1
Biller - resubmits corrected CO-16 and CO-4 claims and must not be blocked, redirected, or given a ready action by the CO-50 gate
PFS lead - sees counts by CARC class and the read-only ready-attempt audit log; has no ready action and no override
Coder - owns modifiers and diagnosis pointers; opens denial detail read-only, receives no CPT or ICD suggestion, and has no ready action
Front desk - reads eligibility only; the denial workqueue route is absent for this role
inScope: A readiness gate on CO-50 denial lines requiring both a non-empty DOC-### clinical-note reference and a filing-deadline date before the line may become appeal-ready
A ready control that is disabled while the gate fails and whose accessible name lists exactly the missing gate items
Enforcement of the gate in one shared domain rule that both the denial detail and the workqueue call, so a forced ready transition is rejected as well as the disabled button

Filing deadline computed as date of service plus 90 days, used for the gate and for the risk band; the remit deadline is used only when the date of service is absent; a mismatch between the two is an advisory, not a block
Per-line gating: the appeal packet is per CO-50 line, and each CO-50 line is gated independently
Verbatim display of the demo-table meaning and the only allowed next action for every code in the table, with unknown codes left unmapped

Workqueue sorted by days remaining with risk bands visible on a closed row, blank deadlines labelled missing and sorted ahead of dated rows, CARC class filter, and a separate patient-responsibility group
Role separation with explicit negative checks for front desk, coder, biller, and PFS lead
A read-only audit entry for every ready attempt, blocked or completed
Synthetic identifiers only, shaped PAT-###, CLM-###, and DOC-###, with the pre-run demo scanner blocking disallowed personal-identifier shapes
outOfScope: Any override, supervisor approval, or force-ready path in v1, including a PFS lead override; no override control is designed, built, or stubbed
Applying the readiness gate to CO-16, CO-197, CO-4, PR-1, or OA-23
Deciding medical necessity, recommending or changing a diagnosis code, suggesting CPT or ICD changes, inventing a modifier, or writing off a balance
Treating the coverage-policy citation as a third gate field in v1; it is an advisory checklist item only
Storing or rendering a clinical note body, attachment, or document content in the clinical-note reference field
Existence checks against a document store for DOC-### values in v1; the check is shape and non-emptiness only
Payer submission of any kind: real plan ids, portals, clearinghouse routes, and the appeal-submitted, upheld, and overturned transitions
Production X12 certification; the demo meanings and fixture remark pairings are confirmed against the current X12 external code list by the product owner before any production use
Any HIPAA determination or business associate agreement; the scanner is a demo scanner

assumptions.text: CO-50 only. CO-16 and CO-197 keep their current path, and no other CARC code gains a gate. On a mixed claim the gate is offered only on the CO-50 line.
Nobody in v1. The ready action stays disabled until both fields are present, and no role - specialist, biller, coder, front desk, or PFS lead - has an override control.
A non-empty DOC-### id. The field is an identifier, not a document body; whitespace-only, free text, and note bodies count as missing.
Date of service plus 90 days. A blank deadline fails the gate.
Name the missing items on the button. The then-clause can be observed from the control's accessible name.

requirements.statement: The readiness gate applies only to CO-50 denial lines. CO-16, CO-197, CO-4, PR-1, and OA-23 keep their current paths and are never gated. On a mixed claim, the gate is offered only on the CO-50 line and must not pull a non-CO-50 line into the appeal packet.
requirements.rationale: Q-1 scopes the gate to CO-50. pack/carc-demo.md gives each code one allowed next action and pack/claim-states.md limits appeal-ready to a CO-50 line, so a class-wide gate would block billers and could turn patient responsibility into a false appeal.

requirements.statement: A CO-50 appeal packet may be marked ready only when both a clinical-note reference and a filing-deadline date are present for that line. If either is absent the ready control is disabled and the line stays in denied. The packet is per CO-50 line; each CO-50 line on a claim is gated independently.
requirements.rationale: CO-50's only allowed next action is: Appeal with the coverage policy and a clinical-note reference. Do not change the diagnosis code in this product. An appeal without the note reference, or without a timely-filing date, is the failure this gate exists to stop (pack/carc-demo.md, pack/payer-northwind.md).

requirements.statement: Nobody may override the gate in v1. The product exposes no override, force-ready, or approve-anyway control to any role, and no justification-to-proceed path exists.
requirements.rationale: Q-2 and pack/roles.md: the denial specialist cannot override the gate in v1 and the PFS lead does not mark packets ready.

requirements.statement: A clinical-note reference counts only when it is a non-empty identifier shaped DOC- followed by exactly three digits in upper case, with no surrounding text. Empty, whitespace-only, free text, lower-case or wrong-length variants, and document bodies count as missing. The field stores and displays the identifier only. In v1 the specialist types the identifier and no existence check is made against a document store.
requirements.rationale: Q-3 and pack/phi-policy.md: allowed identifiers are PAT-###, CLM-###, and DOC-###, and pasting a note body into an identifier field invites disallowed personal data into the demo.

requirements.statement: The filing deadline for a CO-50 line is the date of service plus 90 days, computed by the product and used for both the gate and the risk band. When the date of service is absent, the deadline carried on the remit is used instead. When neither is available the deadline is blank, is labelled missing, and fails the gate. A deadline that is present but already overdue still satisfies the gate and is shown with the overdue risk band. When the remit carried a deadline that differs from the computed date, both dates are shown and the difference is an advisory note; it does not block the gate and no control lets a specialist type a substitute date.
requirements.rationale: Q-4 and pack/payer-northwind.md: timely filing is 90 days from the date of service and a blank deadline is treated as missing. The question round granted only presence-or-blank, so a mismatched-but-present date must not become a release-blocking gate condition.

requirements.statement: While the gate fails, the ready control is disabled and its accessible name is 'Mark appeal packet ready - missing: <items>', naming only the items that are actually missing, using the phrases 'clinical-note reference' and 'filing deadline'. It never shows a generic not-ready message and never names a coverage-policy reference as a missing gate item. When both items are present the control is enabled and named 'Mark appeal packet ready'.
requirements.rationale: Q-5 and pack/patterns/detail-checklist.md: the ready action names each missing item, and naming an item the gate does not check would train specialists to satisfy the wrong checklist.

requirements.statement: The readiness rule lives in one domain module. The denial detail control and the workqueue row call that module and do not reimplement the presence checks. A ready transition invoked on a CO-50 line while either gate item is missing is rejected by the domain rule, the line does not become appeal-ready, and the rejection names the same missing-item phrases an observer reads on the control.
requirements.rationale: pack/patterns/detail-checklist.md says the ready action calls the domain rule and does not reimplement it. A disabled button alone can be bypassed, which is the compliance failure mode of a UI-only gate.

requirements.statement: The denial detail shows the claim lines, the demo-table meaning, and the only allowed next action for the line's code, copied verbatim, plus the appeal checklist. For CO-50 the checklist shows the clinical-note reference and the filing deadline as gate items (present or missing) and the coverage-policy citation as an advisory, non-gating item. An unknown code stays unmapped with no invented meaning and no gate.
requirements.rationale: pack/patterns/detail-checklist.md defines the detail layout and pack/carc-demo.md forbids invented meanings and allows only one next action per code.

requirements.statement: The product offers no control that decides medical necessity, changes or suggests a diagnosis or procedure code, invents a modifier, or writes off a balance, in any state before or after the gate.
requirements.rationale: pack/carc-demo.md states this product does not decide medical necessity and does not recommend a different diagnosis; pack/roles.md bars write-offs and diagnosis changes for everyone in the demo.

requirements.statement: appeal-ready is reachable for a CO-50 line only after the readiness gate passes. A blocked line remains denied, and marking ready never skips the line to appeal-submitted. If a gate item is cleared after a line reaches appeal-ready, the line returns to denied and the ready control is disabled again with the missing item named.
requirements.rationale: pack/claim-states.md allows appeal-ready for a CO-50 line only after the gate passes, and this demo has no payer portal or clearinghouse route (pack/payer-northwind.md).

requirements.statement: The denial workqueue is a dense table of appealable denials with a separate patient-responsibility group, sorted ascending by days remaining to the filing deadline and filterable by CARC class. Against the demo clock of 17 November 2026 the risk band is overdue when days remaining are negative, urgent from 0 through 14 days inclusive, soon from 15 through 45 days inclusive, and comfortable above 45 days. A blank deadline is labelled missing, is never labelled comfortable, and sorts ahead of dated rows. Deadline risk and a blocked/ready marker are visible without opening the row.
requirements.rationale: pack/patterns/workqueue.md and pack/payer-northwind.md make timely-filing risk the queue's safety signal; a blank deadline labelled comfortable is how an untimely CO-50 appeal gets ignored.

requirements.statement: Only the denial specialist may mark a CO-50 packet ready, and only when the gate passes. The front desk has no denial workqueue route at all; the coder may open denial detail read-only from the coding queue; the biller works CO-16 and CO-4 resubmission only; the PFS lead sees counts by CARC class and the audit log. None of these roles has a ready action or an override.
requirements.rationale: pack/roles.md separates denial work from billing, coding, front desk, and PFS oversight, and states the specialist cannot override the gate in v1.

requirements.statement: Every ready attempt on a CO-50 line, blocked or completed, writes an audit entry holding the claim and line identifier, the acting role, the demo timestamp, the outcome, and the missing-item phrases when blocked. The audit log is read-only and visible to the PFS lead; it contains no override field.
requirements.rationale: Resolves the open audit question so the fail-closed gate is reviewable by oversight without giving oversight a way to clear a blocked packet (pack/roles.md).

requirements.statement: Every patient, claim, and document identifier shown or stored by this feature is synthetic and shaped PAT-###, CLM-###, or DOC-###. Intake briefs, diffs, and seed data are scanned before a requirement document is written for a social security number shaped ###-##-####, an email address, a phone number, a raw MRN followed by an identifier, and a date labelled as a date of birth; a hit blocks the run. The scanner is a demo scanner, not a HIPAA determination, and the project does not offer a business associate agreement.
requirements.rationale: pack/phi-policy.md defines the allowed identifiers, the blocking pre-run scanner, and the explicit limits of that scanner.

requirements.statement: The CARC meanings and fixture remark pairings shown in the product carry a visible provenance note stating that they are shortened demo text that the product owner must confirm against the current X12 external code list before any production use, and that an unknown code stays unmapped.
requirements.rationale: pack/carc-demo.md requires both lists to be confirmed against the current X12 external code list before production use and forbids inventing a meaning.

screens.title: Denial workqueue
screens.purpose: Dense table of appealable denials sorted by days remaining to the filing deadline, with the CARC class filter, the risk band, a blank-deadline 'missing' label sorted first, and a blocked or ready marker visible on the closed row. Patient-responsibility lines sit in a separate group and OA-23 is not worked as a denial, so CO-16, CO-4, CO-197, PR-1, and OA-23 keep their current paths.

screens.title: CO-50 denial detail and appeal checklist
screens.purpose: Shows the claim lines, the demo-table meaning and the only allowed next action verbatim, and the appeal checklist with the two gate items plus the advisory coverage-policy item. Hosts the ready control, which calls the shared domain rule, names each missing item when disabled, and exposes no override, diagnosis-change, substitute-date, or write-off control.

screens.title: Oversight: CARC class summary, ready-attempt audit log, and CARC provenance
screens.purpose: Read-only oversight for the PFS lead: counts by CARC class including the blocked CO-50 count, the audit log of blocked and completed ready attempts, and the provenance note on the demo CARC table. The screen deliberately carries no ready action and no override, so oversight cannot clear a blocked packet.
